{
  "title": "Why Some People Go Quiet in the Middle of a Conflict",
  "hook_family": "recognition",
  "hook": "Ever noticed someone freeze in the middle of an argument?",
  "curiosity": "They don’t lash out. They don’t speak. They just… stop. It’s not submission. It’s not silence. It’s something else. Something deep. Something that happens before the mind even knows it’s in danger.",
  "psychological_mechanism": "In the heat of conflict, the brain’s survival instincts kick in. A part of the nervous system called the dorsal vagal complex may activate, slowing the body down, dimming awareness, and disconnecting from the present. It’s a primal response—an attempt to avoid harm by withdrawing, not fighting. It’s not about being passive. It’s about being overwhelmed.",
  "realization": "This is not weakness. It’s not a choice. It’s a reflex. A self-protective reflex that can feel like failure. But understanding this can help you recognize when someone else is not choosing silence—it’s their body speaking in a language you may not yet know.",
  "final_line": "Listen more. Judge less. There’s a story behind the silence.",
  "visual_metaphor": "A person standing in a rainstorm, arms wrapped tightly around themselves, eyes closed, as the rain falls around them—but they’re not moving."
}
